name: trees
title: Trees and shrubs: every tree in the lidar, catalogued trees first, and the shrubs

sources.name: sentinel2
sources.license: Copernicus Sentinel data (free, full and open use)

commands.name: trees-load
commands.help: load a trees build made in the worker image into the database (--build DIR)

commands.name: shrubs-load
commands.help: load a shrubs build made in the worker image into the database (--build DIR)

commands.name: shrubs-hedge-check
commands.help: check the shrubs against OpenStreetMap's hedges (prints a report; writes nothing)

storage: Small: about 60 trees per hectare where there is canopy (the North End box: about 15,000 rows), and 6 to 570 shrubs per hectare (about 340,000 rows for the ten test boxes); each build's files stay in $TVT_ARCHIVE/trees/<build>/ (trees: GeoJSON and a log; shrubs: GeoJSON, build.json and a 0.5 m why.tif).
ethics: Our own data, derived from public USGS 3DEP lidar, two Sentinel-2 NDVI images (early April and July 2025, for the conifer cue; credit "Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2025"), USDA NAIP (the shrubs' near-infrared) and the crown model fitted on the owner's picks (and the US Forest Service's Urban Tree Database, cited). The shrubs build reads farm's crop cover (public inputs: CSB, CDL and Sentinel-2, credited in its build) only to leave crops alone. OpenStreetMap's hedges (ODbL) are a check on the shrubs, never drawn or stored. No catalogue's attributes are stored here: a catalogue (like the City of Boise's inventory, private) contributes trunk points to the trees build only and is joined by id only on the owner's own site; the shrubs build never reads one.
